_note: THE OLD REGULATOR, LINK 2 of 2 (finale). Spec: home-office office/projects/delves/chains.md. Was duo_MB50a_link2_qst.
THE PLAYER'S PART: carrying the thing he replaced to the one person who values it, and the price is his to push (the Commerce line).
CAUSE (rule 2): MB50a's regulator replaced the old one; Noor sent the old one on with a hauler and asks him to meet it. The thing he carries is the thing his last job made spare.

REWRITTEN 2026-11-10 on place.inherit's retirement (Eliza 2026-11-09): no longer at Noor's site. The hauler's drop and the scrapper are both at this link's own site, so it is pickup (the drop) then talk (the scrapper): not MB50a's craft then talk (rule 1).
Chain-only (deal chain), so it may remember (rule 3). Noor stays on the radio: the same person, which is the point of a chain. Pay: med, the finale pays more than a coda would (rule 6).
FIXED 2026-11-10: Noor's closing radio line ('Keep a share, you've earned it') came off the talk, which cannot carry a say. Her last word in the chain is now the ask in MB50a.

FRANCES 2026-11-10 (reviews/2026-11-10-delve-MB106a.md): rework, findings 1-8 taken, 9 is chain-only (no card owed), 10 kept. Forced pick answered NO: the regulator does not leave whole. He takes it apart and writes it down, so 'Nobody can make them' (MB50a) is answered by someone who means to make it untrue. The scarcity is in the always-heard greeting now; the age is said once, on Noor's radio.

place._theme: A quiet site with a scrapper working it. The board's own request, a new site (every link has a site of its own: place.inherit retired 2026-11-09, his 'If we need it always to run it should be using remote sites and making gaurnteed stuff').

prose.name: Hauling: The Old Regulator on <Planet>
prose.briefing: The crew lead from the water reclaimer sent their old pressure regulator on with a hauler. It's waiting at the drop at the <Place>, where a scrapper wants it.

beats._model: A worn machine part, his or Kim's pick.
beats.name: Old Regulator
beats.objective: Collect the old regulator from the hauler's drop

message.title: Old Regulator
message.text: Heavier than the new one, and stamped with a maker's mark nobody uses any more.

beats.journal: I've got the old pressure regulator from the hauler's drop. I need to find the scrapper at the <Place>.
say: That's the one. It's older than both of us.

beats.objective: Sell the old regulator to the scrapper at the <Place>

person.name: Oskar Lindqvist
hellos: If it's broken, I'll look at it. If it's working, why are you here?

_bio.from: a scrapper who keeps old kit running (his lines)
_bio.why_there: his yard; he buys what nobody else can make any more (his lines)
_bio.wants: to take the old parts apart and write down what's inside, so somebody can make them again (his lines)

greeting: Is that the reclaimer regulator? Let me see. Nobody can make what's inside these any more.

reply: More than most working kit. I'll pay the crew direct, and something for your trouble on top.

exchanges.prompt: Whatever you're about to offer, it's worth more.
reply: It is. Fine. A little more.
Nobody can make the parts inside it any more. Somebody should be able to.

exchanges.prompt: What will you do with it?
reply: Take it apart very slowly, and write down everything I find.

beats.journal: I sold the water reclaimer crew's old regulator to the scrapper at the <Place>. He's paying them direct, and he means to find out what's inside it.

speaker.name: Water Reclaimer Crew
speaker._name: Deliberately MB50a's speaker: the same person on the radio, which is the point of a chain.

broadcast: It's the heavy one. Mind your back, and don't let them have it cheap.
_speech: Noor, MB50a's voice, carried on. The scrapper: dry, delighted by old machines; a stand-in voice, his ear decides.
